texts.preamble: Date Of Institution: 07.11.2013 vs M/S Natraj Fasion Knitt Fabrics on 22 May, 2023 In The Court Of Mr. Satyabrata Panda, Adj-04, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cs (Comm) No.361 Of 2019
texts.facts: The plaintiff has filed the present suit against the defendants for permanent injunction and other reliefs in respect of infringement of trademarks and passing off. It is stated that the plaintiff is a limited partnership having its principal CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.1 place of business in New York, USA. The Plaintiff is engaged in the business of manufacture, distribution and sale of a wide range of apparel & clothing for men, women and children (more broadly menswear, womenswear, childrenswear), clothing accessories, hats, leather goods, shoes, furs, luggage and luxurious home dcor including, towels, area rugs, wall coverings and tabletop and table coverings, sportswear, footwear, fragrances, eyewear, fashion accessories, house wares, jewellery, and other allied/related products (hereinafter referred to as the said goods and business). Ever since its bona fide adoption of the Trade Mark Date Of Institution: 07.11.2013 vs M/S Natraj Fasion Knitt Fabrics on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114616406/ 1 POLO in the year 1967, the Plaintiff has subsequently been using the formative POLO marks word per se and in stylized manner in conjunction with other marks/words and device of polo player (hereinafter collectively referred to as the said Trade Mark/Label) in relation to its said goods and business in the course of Trade. In addition to word per se user of the said Trade Mark POLO, the Plaintiff, over a period of time has been using its formative trade mark in conjunction with other words/marks, in various stylized and artistic formats with and/or without the device of polo player, which have been created and are being created over a period of time, viz: POLO, POLO BY RALPH LAUREN, POLO RALPH LAUREN, POLO DENIM, POLO GOLF, POLO JEANS CO., POLO SPORTS, RALF LAUREN, RALF BY RALF LAUREN, RUGBY RALF LAUREN, LAUREN BY RALF LAUREN, RALF LAUREN GOLF and Polo Player Device etc. The true representation of the same has been given as herein below: CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.2 It is stated that the word/mark POLO remains a key and material part thereof. The word/mark POLO has all the trappings of an invented mark and as such are extremely strong mark. 3. It is further stated in the plaint that the word/mark POLO is also most essential feature of the plaintiff's trading style/trade name namely "The Polo/Lauren Company L.P.". The plaintiff has filed the true representations of Plaintiff's said Trade Mark/Label/Trade Name as Annexure-A (Colly.) to the plaint. It is stated that the said Trade Mark/Label/Trade Name of the Plaintiff has all the trappings of an invented and an arbitrary Trade Mark.
texts.arguments: It is further stated in the plaint that the Plaintiff's said products are available in almost all the parts of the world, which is inclusive of India. The Plaintiff has been expanding its said activity in other countries of the world. 11. It is further stated in the plaint that the Plaintiff maintains the highest standard of quality in relation to its goods and business under the said Trade Mark/Label/Trade Name. That the Plaintiff invests heavily in R & D and its products are known for their highest standards of quality, safety innovation and reliability and there is an ever-increasing demand therefore. The Products of the Plaintiff has been widely recognized throughout the world for excellence in the creation of CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.10 contemporary clothing designs. The Plaintiff has received many awards for designs which have been mentioned in the plaint. 12. It is further stated in the plaint that substantial reputation and goodwill has accrued to the POLO Trademarks through extensive use and advertising worldwide. The Plaintiff carries on an established international business as a manufacturer and merchant of a wide variety of consumer merchandise including readymade garments, hosiery, perfumes, other cosmetic goods, home furnishings, sports goods, etc. Over the past 30 years, the Plaintiff has expanded its line of clothing, accessories, fragrances and home furnishings into worldwide markets and is presently recognized as one of the world's market leaders in the designing, marketing and distribution of lifestyle products. By virtue of operation of Section 29 (4) of the Trade Marks Act 1909, any use of identical/similar Trade Mark/Label by any other party in relation to even different business CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.12 and services does amount to violation of plaintiff's aforementioned rights, which is not permissible in law. 16. It is further stated in the plaint that in view of the Plaintiff's proprietary rights both statutory and common law in its said Trade Mark/Label/Trade Name/Domain Name, its goodwill & reputation, and its copyrights, the plaintiff has the exclusive right to the use thereof and nobody can be permitted to use the same or any other deceptively similar Trade Mark/Label/Trade Name/Domain Name thereto in any manner whatsoever in relation to any specification of goods without the leave and license of the Plaintiff. 17. The Defendants have no rights to use it in any manner in relation to its impugned goods and business or for any other specification of goods and business whatsoever being in violation CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.14 of the Plaintiff's aforementioned rights. It is stated that the Plaintiff's said Trade Mark/Label/Trade Name/Domain Name has a strong and wide reputation including in India. It is stated that by virtue of operation of Section 29 (4) of the Trade Marks Act 1999 also the impugned activities of the Defendants under the impugned products do amount to infringement of the Plaintiff's registered Trade Marks. 23. It is further stated in the plaint that due to the Defendants impugned activities, the Plaintiff is suffering huge losses both in business and in reputation and such losses are incapable of being assessed in monetary terms. Unwary purchasers and traders are being deceived as to the origin of goods or business. The Defendants' gains are Plaintiff's losses. The Plaintiff has no access to the Defendants' accounts and the Defendants are liable to render their accounts to the Plaintiff and to make good to the Plaintiff the profits and business earned by them. 24. It is further stated in the plaint that apart from the sales to the direct customers from their respective Shop/Premises the Defendants are supplying the impugned goods bearing the impugned Trade Mark/Label to the dealers/retailers/ distributors in the markets of New Delhi Area viz. Connaught Place, Gole Market, Bengal Market, CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.16 Chankyapuri, Mandir Marg etc. who then supply the impugned goods bearing the impugned Trade Mark/Label to the various unscrupulous traders and manufacturers of the counterfeit products of the Plaintiff which eventually causes confusion and deception to the consumers at large. 25. The ld. counsel for the plaintiff has submitted that the plaintiff has proved its case on the basis of the ex parte evidence led. It is submitted that there is no defence by the defendants and the pleadings as well as evidence of the plaintiff is unrebutted and uncontroverted. It is submitted that as such the plaintiff would be entitled to decree in terms of the prayer clauses of the plaint. It is further submitted that the defendants have deliberately avoided the proceedings and have also prevented the seizure of the goods by the local commissioner. It is submitted that the defendants are dealing in counterfeiting and unfair trade practices. It is submitted that the defendants cannot be permitted to take advantage of their own wrong and that the case calls for punitive damages. Reliance is placed on LT Foods Ltd. v. Saraswati Trading Co. 2022/DHC/004806. 31. As held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Microsoft Corporation Vs.Rajendra Pawar and Anr. reported as2008 (36) PTC 697 (Del.), awarding punitive damages prevents the erring party from taking advantage of its own wrong by escaping prosecution or detection. Reference in this regard is also made to LT Foods Ltd. v. Saraswati Trading Co. 2022/DHC/004806, Proctor & Gamble Company v. Joy Creators 2011 (450) PTC 541 Del, Louis Vuitton Malletier Vs. Iqbal Singh 2019 SCC online DEL 7879: (2019) 258 DLT 760, and Whatman International Ltd Vs. P. Mehta and Ors, 2019 SCC online Del 6856: (2019) 257 DLT 472. The local CS (COMM) NO.361/19 THE POLOLAUREN CO. L.P VS. NATRAJ FASION KNITT FABRICS page no.22 commissioner could not make the seizures as he was prevented from doing so.
